_readme: Cross-language conformance fixture for the resume handle of a provider whose session is a
FILE. Pi is the one such provider today.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the worker enforces the rule (backend/internal/worker/agent/
provider.go, piProvider.ValidateResumeHandle) and the browser hand-mirrors it
(frontend/src/lib/validate.ts, validateSessionFileHandle) so the resume field can refuse a
bad handle at the field instead of after a round trip. The two copies drifted once and the
drift removed the feature: the browser applied the TOKEN rule to every provider, so it
refused a real Pi session path at the 128-byte cap, while the worker applied the PATH rule
to Pi, so it refused the session ID the browser accepted with 'path must be absolute'.
Neither shape of handle could be submitted. Both suites read this file, so editing one
side without the other turns that side's CI red.
TWO SHAPES, ONE FIELD. Pi identifies one session two ways and `pi --session <path|id>`
resolves both: a value that holds a separator or ends in `.jsonl` is a session file path,
and anything else is a session ID matched inside the working directory's session
directory. Both sides pick the rule with that same shape test, so a handle is validated
against the rule that describes what will happen to it. A bare `~` therefore takes the
TOKEN rule on both sides: it holds no separator.
THE BROWSER IS DELIBERATELY NARROWER, AND ONLY IN ONE DIRECTION. It refuses only what is
wrong on every host -- a relative path, a `..` escape, a value past the byte cap -- and
leaves the reserved device names and the OS-specific spelling of 'absolute' to the worker,
which knows its own host. So a case may be accepted by the browser and refused by a worker
('the worker decides'), and the OS columns below say which. The reverse is the bug this
file exists to prevent, and BOTH suites assert it: a case the browser refuses must be
refused by every worker column, because a value the browser refuses never reaches a worker
to be judged.
THE OS COLUMNS. `worker.posix` and `worker.windows` are what SanitizePath answers on that
host: filepath.IsAbs reads a POSIX root on POSIX and a drive or UNC root on Windows, so
one legitimate path is refused by the other host's rule. The Go suite reads the column for
runtime.GOOS; the browser suite reads `browser` and asserts the one-directional invariant
against both columns.
`refusal` is a stable token, not a message: each suite maps it to a substring of its own
wording. `input` is built as head + text*repeat + tail, so an over-cap case stays short
here. `homeDir` is the home directory each host's SanitizePath expands `~` against.

cases.why: the empty handle is accepted and means 'no resume'
a bare session ID is accepted: it holds no separator, so the token rule applies -- the path rule refused this exact value with 'path must be absolute' and that was the launch failure
the POSIX session path Pi reports, 137 bytes: the browser's token cap refused it at 128 and blocked the only value the worker would take
a Windows session path: it holds the backslash the token class bans, so the token rule refused it as well
a UNC path is absolute on Windows and is not a path at all on POSIX
a tilde path expands against the home directory on both hosts, so it is the one spelling that resumes everywhere
a bare tilde holds no separator, so BOTH sides read it as an ID and the token rule accepts it -- Pi then reports that it names no session
the .jsonl suffix makes a bare file name a PATH, and a bare file name is relative
a relative path is refused: the worker resolves it against the agent process's directory, which is not where sessions live
a `..` escape is refused after the tilde expands, on every host
the same escape written POSIX-absolute: Windows answers the absolute question first, which is why the refusal token is per host
a path past the 1024-byte file-path cap is refused before it is parsed
the ID shape keeps the 128-byte TOKEN cap: the larger cap belongs to the path shape alone
the ID shape keeps the argv rule, because the worker hands the handle to `pi --session <id>` as its own argv element
the ID shape keeps the character class: a control character names no session
whitespace alone is neither shape, and the token rule reports the edge rule for it
